data.name: Dharma
data.gender_notes: Dharma is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The moral principle which governs human actions and the order and regularity of the universe. It is the fundamental principle of the universe, and the moral duty of an individual. The name Dharma carries the meaning “Duty, Law, Order” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dharma usually hope their child will grow to embody duty, law, order and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The divine law that sustains the universe and guides our actions.
data.etymology: Dharma belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Duty, Law, Order.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dharma total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_sanskrit.name: धर्म:
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The moral principle which is the essential nature of the universe and which regulates all the actions and behaviors of living beings. Dharma also refers to the cosmic order and law, which is the foundation of the universe and which governs all phenomena in the universe.

in_hindi.name: धर्म:
in_hindi.long_meaning: धर्ता (holder, supporter): A person who upholds righteousness and supports the social order. धर्मशास्त्र (scripture of duties): The scriptures that lay down the rules of conduct for different sections of society. धर्मनिरत (righteous): A person who is always devoted to dharma, i.e., duty, righteousness, and moral order.

in_tamil.name: தர்ம:
in_tamil.long_meaning: தரும் (support): The foundation or support that holds things together. அறியல் (understanding, knowledge): The knowledge and understanding of the righteous path and the cosmic order. அவற்றையு் செய்யும் (practicing, doing): The practice and implementation of the righteous path and the cosmic order. வித்தியால் (wisdom): The wisdom that comes from understanding and practicing dharma.

in_telugu.name: ధర్మ:
in_telugu.long_meaning: ధర్మపేద (supporter): A person who supports and upholds righteousness and moral order. ధర్మశాస్త్ర (scripture of duties): The scriptures that lay down the rules of conduct for different sections of society. ధర్మనిర్దేశ (righteous): A person who is always devoted to dharma, i.e., duty, righteousness, and moral order.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Dharma" holds immense cultural significance in Hinduism, as it embodies the concept of righteous living, duty, and moral responsibility towards oneself and society. It governs various aspects of Hindu life, from social norms to religious practices. Dharma includes respect for ancestors, virtuous conduct, attendance to one's duties, honesty, and non-violence. It emphasizes the importance of preserving the order and balance in society through adherence to ethical and moral principles.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, "Dharma" signifies the divine order and the moral law that governs the cosmos and individual souls. It implies following the path of righteousness, truth, and self-realization, and is considered essential for attaining moksha or liberation from the cycle of birth and death. The pursuit of Dharma connects an individual to their true self and to the divine, fostering inner peace, contentment, and harmony.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dharma represents moral duty, righteousness, and cosmic law in Hinduism. It is the fundamental pillar of individual and societal sustenance, guiding us to fulfill our duties towards ourselves, others, and the universe.

vedic_reference.note: Dharma is a fundamental concept in Hinduism and is mentioned frequently in the Vedas, Upanishads, and other Hindu scriptures. It is considered to be the foundation of the universe and the source of all moral and ethical values.
